newsitem.title: INDIA: India SBI to review loan rates in April.
newsitem.headline: India SBI to review loan rates in April.

text.p: The State Bank of India (SBI) will review its prime lending rate (PLR) in April after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) announces its six-month credit policy, chairman P.G. Kakodkar was quoted on Tuesday as saying.
"We think the right time to take a decision on the PLR would be after the RBI slack season credit policy is available," the United News of India (UNI) quoted Kakodkar as saying.
With the financial year 1996/97 about to end on March 31, the time was not proper to announce a change in lending rates, he said while opening a bank branch in New Delhi.
"If we change the PLR now, it will create a lot of confusion at the branch level," he said.

The RBI is expected to announce its credit policy sometime in the first half of April. Indian officials say commercial banks have substantial funds. Industrial lobbies have been calling for a cut in lending rates.
State-run SBI is India's largest commercial bank.
SBI will soon apply to the government for setting up a brokerage subsidiary, SBI Securities, and announce next week the launch of a new subsidiary for credit cards, Kakodkar said.
In view of a shortage of funds faced by Indian companies, SBI was willing to relax debt-equity ratios for borrowers, UNI quoted SBI managing director, M.S. Verma, as saying.
